extractionNotes: COMPLETE: full re-extraction of all 3 Strands / 21 Sub-Strand-Year instances / 26 Learning Outcomes / 24 Content Standards / 62 Learning Indicators across SHS 1-3, replacing an earlier interrupted attempt that had written only 1 Learning Outcome and 2 Learning Indicators before an account rate limit cut it short. This file was written incrementally, Strand by Strand, per extraction-task instructions, to survive further interruptions.

Page/pdfPageIndex methodology: the full document text (PDF pages 22-123, i.e. printed pages 20-121) was extracted once via 'pdftotext -f 22 -l 123 -layout' and every printed-page footer ('<n> | ART AND DESIGN STUDIO' or 'ART AND DESIGN STUDIO | <n>') was located by exact line number, alongside every curriculum code's line number. Each node's page = the printed-page number of the NEXT footer encountered after that node's own code/heading in the raw text stream (a consistent 'footer-after' rule applied uniformly across the whole document). pdfPageIndex = printed page + 2 throughout (confirmed offset, matching the prior inventory pass and the previously-written placeholder for this file). Because the source uses a multi-column table layout that pdftotext's -layout mode does not always reconstruct in strict visual order across a page break (columns from the bottom of one page and the top of the next are sometimes interleaved in the raw text stream), page attribution for individual rows within a table that spans a page break is a consistent best-effort convention, not a guaranteed pixel-exact value; content text itself is unaffected by this and was transcribed verbatim regardless of which page it was ultimately attributed to.

Document structure: SCOPE AND SEQUENCE summary table (printed page 22-23) is badly garbled under plain-text extraction -- Sub-Strand labels and per-year CS/LO/LI count columns run together on merged/misaligned lines. It was NOT used as a source of truth for per-Sub-Strand counts; only the table's overall grand totals (Content Standards 24, Learning Outcomes 26, Learning Indicators 62 across SHS 1-3) were used, and those grand totals were independently verified by summing every Content Standard/Learning Outcome/Learning Indicator actually extracted below -- the totals match exactly (24/26/62; per-year breakdown Year1 = 8 CS/10 LO/19 LI, Year2 = 8 CS/8 LO/21 LI, Year3 = 8 CS/8 LO/22 LI).

This document uses the header 'Teaching and Learning Materials' (abbreviated 'TLMs' inline) rather than 'Teaching and Learning Resources' (TLR) as seen in Physics/Robotics/Biomedical Science -- a genuine cross-subject terminology difference, recorded verbatim via teachingLearningResourcesHeaderSeen on every Sub-Strand.

The GESI/SEL column header carries footnote markers on first use per Year (e.g. 'GESI1, SEL2 and Shared National Values' in Year One, 'GESI3, SEL4...' in Year Two, 'GESI5, SEL6...' in Year Three, each followed by footnotes '1/3/5 Gender Equality and Social Inclusion' / '2/4/6 Socio-Emotional Learning' at the foot of the page); on later rows within the same Year the header sometimes reprints as plain 'GESI, SEL and Shared National Values' without digits once the footnote has already been defined on an earlier page. The exact header text seen is preserved verbatim per Learning Outcome via gesiSelHeaderSeen.

Teaching and Learning Materials grids at the end of Sub-Strand blocks (and, in several Sub-Strands with two Content Standards, also mid-block between the two Content Standards) are printed as multi-column bullet tables that wrap unpredictably across the extracted text layout, with items from different visual columns frequently interleaved onto the same line and column headers/footers occasionally bleeding into the item list (e.g. 'Teaching and Learning problems.' where the CS description's trailing word 'problems.' collided with the TLM row label). Item lists below were reconstructed conservatively in left-to-right, top-to-bottom reading order from the -layout text; exact original column grouping could not be reliably reconstructed and is not claimed.

Strand and Sub-Strand name spelling/casing genuinely varies by Year in the source (preserved verbatim per Year, per canonical-schema design note on Strand names): Strand 1 prints as 'ART AND DESIGN THEORIES AND APPLICATION' in Years One and Three but 'ART & DESIGN THEORIES AND APPLICATION' (ampersand) in Year Two. Sub-Strand 'Material Classifications and Methods' (Y1, plural 'Classifications') appears as 'Material Classifications and methods' (Y2, mixed case) and 'Material Classification and Methods' (Y3, singular 'Classification'). Sub-Strand 'Thinking Studio' prints ALL CAPS in Years One/Two but title-case 'Thinking Studio' in Year Three. Sub-Strand 'Portfolio Building' prints ALL CAPS in Years One/Two but title-case 'Portfolio Building' in Year Three. These are recorded as printed per year; not flagged NEEDS_REVIEW individually as they are casing/formatting variance rather than content errors.

GENUINE CODE ANOMALY (Year 2, Strand 2, Sub-Strand 1 'THINKING STUDIO'): the Learning Outcome and Content Standard are correctly coded 2.2.1.LO.1 / 2.2.1.CS.1, but all three of that Content Standard's Learning Indicators and Assessment items are printed with the code prefix '2.3.1' instead of '2.2.1' (i.e. '2.3.1.LI.1/2/3' and '2.3.1.AS.1/2/3'). This is a genuine printed-source error, verified directly in the raw extracted text (PDF printed pages 69-71), preserved verbatim. It also creates a real code COLLISION, because '2.3.1' is independently and correctly the code prefix for Year 2 / Strand 3 (CREATIVE PROJECT) / Sub-Strand 1 (ARTEFACT PRODUCTION), whose own Learning Indicators are also printed as 2.3.1.LI.1/2/3 (printed pages 81-83) with entirely different content (protective/decorative processes in artefact production, vs. mixed-media ideations of antique cultural products for the Thinking Studio sub-strand). Both sets of nodes are flagged NEEDS_REVIEW with cross-references.

GENUINE DATA ISSUE (Year 2, Strand 2, Sub-Strand 2 'FABRICATION AND CONSTRUCTION', Content Standard 2.2.2.CS.2, printed pages 77-78): the Assessment code '2.2.2.AS.2' is printed twice (once adjacent to Learning Indicator 2.2.2.LI.2's first Pedagogical Exemplar block, and again adjacent to a later Pedagogical Exemplar block for the same LI.2), and no '2.2.2.AS.3' code is printed anywhere for Learning Indicator 2.2.2.LI.3 (whose DoK descriptor block is present in the text but with no visible Assessment code label attached). Preserved verbatim; flagged NEEDS_REVIEW.

GENUINE TYPO (Year 3, Strand 2, Sub-Strand 2 'FABRICATION AND CONSTRUCTION', Content Standard 3.2.2.CS.2, printed pages 111-113): all three Learning Indicators are printed as '3.2.2.L1.1', '3.2.2.L1.2', '3.2.2.L1.3' -- using the digit '1' in place of the letter 'I' in 'LI' -- rather than '3.2.2.LI.1/2/3' used everywhere else in the document. Preserved verbatim as printed; flagged NEEDS_REVIEW as an evident source typo, not corrected.

Pedagogical Exemplars chunking convention: each distinct named-pedagogy paragraph (e.g. 'Talk for Learning:', 'Project-Based Learning:', 'Group Work/Collaborative Learning:') is stored as one array entry; where the source further breaks a single named pedagogy into multiple bulleted sub-points, those sub-points are joined into that same entry (verbatim wording preserved, only the bullet glyphs removed) rather than split into separate array entries, for extraction-pace reasons. This is a chunking-granularity choice, not a content change.

Front matter (PDF pages 1-24 approx., printed pages i-22): shared SHS boilerplate covering THE SHS CURRICULUM OVERVIEW/INTRODUCTION, PHILOSOPHY/VISION/GOAL of Art and Design Studio, the Curriculum Development Panel list (writers, reviewers, NaCCA team, external QA team), and the Scope-and-Sequence summary table -- not re-extracted per-node per the schema's Phase 5 design notes (document-level context, not curriculum-tree content). Not re-verified in this pass beyond what was already captured in the prior inventory pass (which noted a leftover/garbled title-block artifact from an unrelated 'PHYSICAL AND HEALTH EDUCATION...BASIC 7-10' template bleeding through the cover page -- a shared production artifact across the SHS PDF batch, not part of Art and Design Studio's own content).

Overall totals cross-check: this extraction captures 24 Content Standards, 26 Learning Outcomes, and 62 Learning Indicators across SHS 1-3, matching the Scope and Sequence table's stated grand totals exactly.

learningOutcomes.description: Analyse the scope and role of Art and Design Studios in Ghanaian society.

guidance.twentyFirstCenturySkills: Collaboration and Communication; Digital literacy: Learners develop an awareness of the meaning and major scopes of Art and Design studio practices through research and dissemination. Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Digital Literacy: Learners develop the ability to use available technologies in solving problems in society as they reflect on various fields under fine art and applied art and their respective career opportunities in groups to create a chart/legend/video presentation. Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving Digital Literacy: Learners acquire the skills to think critically and to solve problems using the available technologies as they analyse the scope of common methods in Art and Design and their respective career opportunities. Collaboration and Communication; Digital Literacy; Cultural identity: Learners develop skills in communication and cultural identity as they analyse the roles of Art and Design studio practices in the training of student-artists. Learners acquire the skill of collaboration and cultural identity as they brainstorm with others to generate ideas and solutions on the concept of an art studio and what it entails as well as how it is used in the making of artworks. Learners develop the skill of communicating with others and using available technologies to process information as they question the lives of the professional artists and artist residence programmes and relate it to their cultural identity for presentation. Collaboration and Communication; Digital Literacy; Cultural identity: Learners develop the skill of communicating with others and using available technologies to process information research as they discuss and make presentations on the roles of Art and Design studio practices in the training of student-artists. Collaboration and Communication; Digital Literacy; Critical Thinking, Creative Thinking and Problem-Solving: Learners develop the skill of communicating and thinking critically to generate solutions to problems as they search to identify and present art studio tools and materials, the safety precautions and how they are used.
guidance.gesi: GESI: Providing the opportunity for diverse learners with different abilities and from different backgrounds to actively participate in all lessons inclusively and using GESI responsive language as pedagogy ensures; awareness of personal biases and stereotypes in analysing the scope of common methods in Art and Design. respect and tolerance for an individual's uniqueness and peculiarities. sensitivity to the interrelatedness of the various spheres of life, groups and individuals.
guidance.sel: SEL: Creating opportunities for learners to build their Social Emotional Learning Competencies - Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, Relationship Skills and Responsible Decisions are integrated throughout all lessons to encourage inclusion. As part of achieving each learning outcome in the curriculum, the teacher should apply the social-emotional learning strategies to ensure that learners are: self-reflecting and finding confidence; exhibiting motivation, and SMART goal setting; managing emotions and conflicts; showing empathy and cooperation. These may be done by the teacher through modelling emotional self-regulation and decision-making, and the promotion of positive self-talk with self-made portraits, as learners analyse the scope and role of Art and Design Studios in Ghanaian society.

They also acquire skills in modifying existing work or creating new analogue and digital works as solutions for challenges/problems in different contexts. Learners also acquire the habit of engaging cultural contexts and environmental conditions for local remedies so they can work with multiple materials and methods. Critical digital skills like photoshoots, scanning, and photocopying, as well as web crawling, are also developed. Visual Literacy and Creativity; Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Glocal Citizenship and Responsibility; Digital Literacy and Resourcefulness: Learners acquire the skill of associating professional objects, equipment and accoutrements with production capabilities of various art and design practices. Learners learn to improve and modify dated tools with objects, equipment and accoutrements that speak 21st Century language with digital technology and media. Visual Literacy and Creativity; Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Glocal Citizenship and Responsibility: Learners develop skills to associate professional objects, equipment and accoutrements with production capabilities of various art and design practices with realia, pointing to specifics of form. They acquire habits of creating complex pictorial representations of professions and tools, and methods of their creation, including professions outside the community with digital media. Learners develop associated presentational skills for professional objects, equipment and accoutrements through circulating images of the subject. They acquire skills in creating complex pictorial representations for the likes of scrapbooks and visual dairies. This leads to the awareness of the form of objects and presentation format in different contexts. Learners develop analytic skills in breaking down complex objects and formulas to arrive at the basics. They develop the ability to innovate and think creatively, building on their knowledge base to achieve new goals associated with professional objects, equipment and accoutrements. Learners develop skills in combining different materials, resulting in innovative methods of production in the various art and design practices through an understanding of subject content and application in different contexts. They acquire habits of working from samples gleaned from pictorial representations. Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Visual Literacy and Creativity; Glocal Citizenship and Responsibility; Digital Literacy and Resourcefulness: Learners acquire the ability to categorise art and design works according to complex combinations of production processes. Understand subject application in different contexts through the continuous use of a variety of digital technologies and manual processes. Learners develop the ability to observe and proffer art and design solutions to societal problems, especially those within the local community. They evolve sensibilities that result in protocols that afford them opportunities to participate in and address observed challenges in the glocal environment. Learners develop the ability to propose and compete with peers with art and design solutions with discarded materials in the environment. They evolve protocols and technical skills that afford them opportunities to participate in and address observed challenges in the glocal environment.
